proof_summary: For each bound $B$, only finitely many pairs $(p,q)$ with $p$ prime, $q>0$, and $\phi(p)\phi(q)\le B$ exist: bounded totient forces bounds on every prime divisor and its exponent, hence on the integer itself. Choosing $n>2$ outside the finite set of sums $p+q$ of such pairs, the assumed decomposition yields a prime $(\phi(p)\phi(q))^4+1>B$, so primes of the required form are arbitrarily large.
